notes: Dedicated native renderer: all fifteen properties, five events, the default slot and fourteen appearance hooks. Direct-child ownership, exclusive and keep-one coordination, heading/region presentation, pointer and keyboard reorder, lifted clipping, reorder motion, interaction states, drop-placeholder paint and the floating panel are checked against Chrome oracles.

Floating mode: the nearest AWCAccordionViewport or the window root (insets are not subtracted) stands in for the CSS viewport. Compose zIndex orders a panel only among siblings of its container, whereas CSS position: fixed stacks against the whole document.

drop-placeholder is rendered natively and styled through the five drop-placeholder appearance fields; native views accept no ::part declarations for it. Dash centres drift along the border path by up to 1.20 px (open).
Android Compose rendering, events, retained-host and device suites are recorded; TalkBack delivery and OS accessibility traversal remain unverified.

Dedicated native item: all ten properties, three events, toggle() and focusHeader() through AWCAccordionItemControllerScope, four slots, twenty-four appearance hooks and eleven typed part targets. mdItemRequestFocus and mdItemRequestReorder bubble to the owning accordion, which performs the source navigation and keyboard reorder.
An item that is not a direct child of an accordion is never owned and keeps its own disclosure state and events, like the source element.
chassis-handle and chassis-handle-bar render on the first item of a floating accordion and are styled through chassisHandleColor and chassisHandleBackgroundHover; they accept no part declarations.
Android Compose rendering, events, retained-host and device suites are recorded; TalkBack delivery and OS accessibility traversal remain unverified.

Native Material/Compose appearance; CSS selectors, DOM APIs, browser form APIs, cancelable DOM events and source imperative methods are not compiled. Unsupported source properties are reported by the compiler.

Dedicated native chart (the ported md-chart engine drawn on a SwiftUI Canvas / Compose DrawScope): every property, the legend, tooltips, hover layer, keyboard cursor and its live announcement, drag and slider zoom, entrance / drill / follow motion, the header, footer, empty and loader slots, and every event.

Formatter and renderer closures (valueFormatter, tooltipRenderer) go through AWCChartFormatters + .awcChartFormatters (SwiftUI) / ChartFormatters + LocalAWCChartFormatters (Compose), keyed by node id; hooks through AWCChartAppearance; methods through AWCChartController (toDataURL returns the canvas layer as a PNG data URL; getInstance has no native counterpart — it returns the Web engine object).

macOS SwiftUI, the iOS simulator and the Android emulator are verified against Chrome 153: paint scenes, hover / keyboard / pointer and state replays with events, entrance motion per frame, slots, RTL.

Native Material/Compose appearance; CSS selectors, DOM APIs, browser form APIs, cancelable DOM events and source imperative methods are not compiled. Unsupported source properties are reported by the compiler.

Automatically registers with AWCFormScope for native name/required rules, successful-control data and reset. Declarative text rules use AWCFormRules; native regex/type and browser UI limitations remain explicit.

Dedicated native avatar: all eleven properties (image → initials → default slot → person icon; size presets with density 0…−4 and custom CSS lengths: unitless px, px, rem, em, vw, vh, vmin, vmax, pt, pc, in, cm, mm, q with calc/min/max/clamp; circle, rounded and square shapes with physical corners), mdLoad/mdError with { src }, the default slot, twenty-five appearance hooks and three typed part targets.

Identity as in the source: explicit initials (trimmed, three graphemes, locale upper-case) or the first and last name tokens; the name palette bucket uses the source's JavaScript hash; role img with the label, alt or name, otherwise hidden from assistive technology.
As in the source, a name palette wins over containerColor/labelColor (they color neutral avatars); the fourteen palette hooks (missing from the CEM) recolor their own bucket.

Images decode natively from data:, file: and http(s) sources; loading=lazy has no viewport deferral and crossorigin has no CORS semantics (a crossorigin change re-requests a displayed image, as Chrome does). Inline SVG slot content has no native equivalent; native views go in the slot.
macOS SwiftUI/AppKit and Android emulator renderers are verified against the Chrome oracles; iOS SDK, simulator/device and VoiceOver/TalkBack execution remain unverified.

Dedicated native badge implements all six source properties, the authored icon slot and ten typed appearance hooks. AWCBadgeHost uses the actual parent size for physical top-right rect/circle anchors; offsets combine native lengths with fractions of badge size. Explicit empty icon content suppresses fallback. Native layout and font rasterization replace CSS/browser rendering; runtime acceptance is recorded separately in the parity audit.

Dedicated native chart (the ported md-chart engine drawn on a SwiftUI Canvas / Compose DrawScope): every property, the legend, tooltips, hover layer, keyboard cursor and its live announcement, drag and slider zoom, entrance / drill / follow motion, the header, footer, empty and loader slots, and every event.

Formatter and renderer closures (valueFormatter, tooltipRenderer) go through AWCChartFormatters + .awcChartFormatters (SwiftUI) / ChartFormatters + LocalAWCChartFormatters (Compose), keyed by node id; hooks through AWCChartAppearance; methods through AWCChartController (toDataURL returns the canvas layer as a PNG data URL; getInstance has no native counterpart — it returns the Web engine object).

macOS SwiftUI, the iOS simulator and the Android emulator are verified against Chrome 153: paint scenes, hover / keyboard / pointer and state replays with events, entrance motion per frame, slots, RTL.

Dedicated native bottom sheet hosted by AWCModalScope: standard (modal, edge-attached) and detached variants; all thirteen properties, mdOpen/mdClose/mdCancel with null payloads, show/close through AWCBottomSheetController (the source has no whenClosed), drag-handle dismissal with the source threshold, all four slots, sixteen appearance hooks and eleven typed part targets.

Shared modal layer: one owner stack for dialogs and sheets (only the top owner handles Escape/back, Tab and scrim dismissal; content under an open modal is inert; focus moves in on open and is restored on close, forwarded when a lower owner closes first) and the source z-index paint order, measured against Chrome in thirteen mixed-stack runs.
Outside an AWCModalScope the component keeps the previous platform presentation (a SwiftUI sheet / a Compose dialog window).
macOS SwiftUI/AppKit and Android emulator renderers are verified against the Chrome oracles; iOS SDK, simulator/device and VoiceOver/TalkBack execution remain unverified.

A link crumb (href, not current, not disabled) or a static span; mdSelect { href, label, current, itemIndex, itemTotal } is cancelable and, unless prevented, the link opens through the host URL router (target honoured; rel has no native browsing-context effect).
collapsed, itemIndex and itemTotal are managed by the trail (as the source sets them); a crumb outside a trail renders as the first crumb and is the current page only when authored.
Hover, press and keyboard focus (12 % layer, 3-point secondary ring) with the md-ripple wave; labels truncate at 32 ch with an ellipsis and keep the full accessible name.

Dedicated native renderer (SwiftUI / Compose): the wrapping list, separators, the collapse window with the overflow toggle, the current-page promotion and the staggered entrance computed from the authored md-breadcrumb-item children, as the source.

expand() / collapse() through AWCBreadcrumbsController emit mdExpand { expanded, itemCount } (cancelable like the source event; the state does not depend on it). The toggle moves focus to the first revealed link.
The twelve hooks through .awcBreadcrumbsAppearance(…) / AWCBreadcrumbsAppearanceScope; density follows the md3 ladder including the rung-only spacing tokens.
macOS SwiftUI, the iOS simulator and the Android emulator are verified against the Mac Chrome 153 oracles (paint, interaction states and motion); the trail is a labelled navigation container.
Native Compose button with explicit forms, cancelable action scopes, safe routing and named content; browser-specific gaps are described in nativeEquivalents.

Dedicated Compose button matches source size/density rules, all five palette/toggle variants, bundled source Roboto and Material Symbols fonts, 200ms press/400ms release corner morph, source pointer-origin ripple timing and polygon loading animation. Real Compose PressInteraction owns press state. Source slots replace icon/label/loader fallbacks. Native form scopes automatically register source field adapters, collect ordered successful entries, apply declarative rules and support vetoable submit/reset and Enter; native action scopes can synchronously cancel defaults or stop scoped propagation; safe application routing carries target metadata. Literal browser form APIs, browser documents/origins, DOM nodes, platform elevation shadows, antialiasing and unrestricted browser ARIA roles remain different. Native groupTabindex supports null/0 sequential entry and -1 omission while preserving native programmatic focus, touch and accessibility actions. Hard-disabled controls are excluded; soft-disabled/loading controls remain focusable and block activation. roleOverride supports button and gridcell; unknown values safely retain Button semantics. Grid cells expose selected state independent of toggle plus explicit AWCGridScope/AWCGridCellScope collection metadata. mdClick reports proposed selected state before commit; mdChange follows commit. DOM originalEvent is omitted. RTL mirroring/expanded rotation currently applies to icon string fallbacks; custom icon slots retain their own transforms. Per-instance CSS custom properties are not evaluated.

HTML_FORM.description: AWC source field adapters register automatically with native form scopes. Shared declarative rules, ordered successful-control entries, duplicate names, multi-values, native Enter/default submission, vetoable submit/reset, initial-state restoration and explicit owner IDs replace the button form contract.
limitations: Native scope ownership replaces ElementInternals; no DOM nodes, browser validation popup or browser network submission is created.
Pattern validation uses Kotlin/Java full-match regular expressions, not the HTML JavaScript v-flag grammar. Native declarative text types cover text, email, URL and number.
Entry order follows native registration order. Applications that reorder retained keyed controls must re-register them when a new data order is required.

SHADOW_DOM.description: Scoped Compose content supplies the button label, leading/trailing icons and loader without a shadow root.
limitations: This is native composition; browser style encapsulation and DOM node access are not exposed.

DOM_QUERY.description: Explicit named-content lookup and injected navigation replace the button-specific anchor and slot queries.
limitations: Arbitrary CSS selectors and DOM traversal are not provided.

SLOT_INTROSPECTION.description: Observable composition replaces slot assignment inspection; adding/removing registered content updates the button and restores absent-slot fallbacks. Legacy content lambdas remain supported.
limitations: Slots contain composables rather than HTMLElement collections. Custom icon content retains its own transforms.

DOM_GLOBAL.description: Safe relative links resolve against the source native context current URL. Observable native contexts implement self, blank, parent, top and reusable named destinations, independent history, back and subtree close. A host can reject navigation before commit and present accepted destinations after commit. Unsafe raw links never fall through to form actions.
limitations: Contexts are native application state, not browser windows, documents, origins or opener relationships; no page is fetched by the coordinator.

Named native destinations are deliberately reusable; source window.open with noopener/noreferrer may instead create fresh browser contexts. Browser modifier/middle-click navigation and window APIs are not reproduced.
URLs must parse as native URIs. Applications supply presentation for coordinator destinations; the legacy default router still opens absolute Android URIs.

CANCELABLE_EVENT.description: Synchronous native capture, target and bubble dispatch uses stable target/path/scope IDs and ordered listeners. Cancelable mdClick runs before defaults, with separate stopPropagation and stopImmediatePropagation controls; committed mdChange is noncancelable. Explicit boundaries and nonbubbling events are supported; legacy callbacks still observe actions after dispatch.
limitations: The event path contains explicit native scopes, not DOM nodes or browser shadow-tree retargeting.
Activation metadata defaults to unknown when the host cannot identify the source; DOM originalEvent, isTrusted, browser modifiers and cancellation of native OS input are not claimed.

notes: Native nowrap layout with source density gaps, connected mixed-button corners, content-box flex sizing, seven typed layout hooks, standard neighbor press motion, ordered selection snapshots and roving focus. Raw click reconciliation runs after child behavior even when child action was canceled or soft-disabled/loading; required can reselect the clicked child. The group emits once per raw click, including unchanged deltas. Nested and wrapped descendants participate in every ancestor group, with shared selected state, inner-to-outer raw-click reconciliation and authored-tree focus order. DOM originalEvent is replaced by actual child activation metadata, not fabricated.

DOM_QUERY.description: Native authored layout-tree traversal includes nested and wrapped descendants; shared selection and inner-to-outer reconciliation preserve ancestor participation. Logical layout direction and roving keyboard focus replace DOM queries.
limitations: Native layout-tree traversal replaces querySelectorAll; arbitrary CSS selector evaluation is not exposed.

DOM_OBSERVER.description: Native button and icon-button children register in measured composition order and retain state across keyed reordering.
limitations: DOM MutationObserver and CSS selectors are replaced by composition and layout lifecycle.

CSS_RUNTIME.api: AWCButtonGroupAppearanceScope / native density and layout values
CSS_RUNTIME.description: Typed native appearance, density and child layout metrics provide the gap, geometry and neighbor-press motion inputs that the Web component reads from computed CSS.
limitations: Arbitrary CSS rules are not evaluated by the native renderer.

CANCELABLE_EVENT.description: mdSelectionChange is dispatched through native action scopes after selection is reconciled, with values, added and removed arrays and actual child activation metadata. Cancellation does not reverse the already committed selection, matching the Web event order.
limitations: Native scope propagation replaces DOM bubbling and composed paths; a browser originalEvent object is not fabricated.

notes: Dedicated native card: all nine properties, mdClick and the three drag events with the source payloads, the default slot, fourteen appearance hooks and two typed part targets (state-layer, outline). The source cascade is followed rule by rule, including pressed styles outranking dragged styles under real pointer input.

The card is a button with a tab stop only when interactive and its content has no interactive controls. Native content cannot be introspected like the DOM: Swift derives this from authored AWC nodes and AWCCardInteractiveRegion, Compose content marks controls with Modifier.awcCardInteractiveContent().
Compose pointer input does not move focus to authored buttons (Chrome focuses a pressed <button>); Material buttons join Tab traversal only in keyboard input mode.
While dragging, the raised stacking (z-index 1000) orders the card only among the siblings of its container; CSS z-index stacks against the document.
The grab/grabbing/pointer cursors and aria-grabbed are not mapped.
Android Compose rendering, events, retained-host and device suites are recorded; TalkBack delivery and OS accessibility traversal remain unverified.
Dedicated native checkbox: all twelve properties (indeterminate, error/errorText, supportingText, density 0…−4), mdChange and mdValidityChange, fourteen appearance hooks and five typed part targets.

Methods through AWCSelectionControlController: getValidity/checkValidity/reportValidity/setCustomValidity follow the source's constraint validation; reportValidity() shows the message in the supporting line and focuses the checkbox.

Click toggles (indeterminate → checked), Space once per press with the pressed pulse and a centred ripple, Enter inert; soft disabled stays focusable; the native form resets checked and indeterminate without events.
macOS SwiftUI/AppKit and Android emulator renderers are verified against the Chrome oracles; iOS runs through the simulator harness; VoiceOver/TalkBack execution remains unverified.

Dedicated native chip: all fourteen properties (assist, filter, input and suggestion variants; outlined, filled and elevated appearances; colour roles; contentAlign; density 0…−4), mdClick, mdSelect and the cancelable mdRemove, the default, leading-icon and trailing-icon slots, twelve appearance hooks and seven typed part targets.
Roles as in the source: a button chip, a group with a primary action and the remove button, and a display token. Enter and Space activate; Delete and Backspace remove.
Lengths: SwiftUI takes px, em, rem and ch (AWCChipLength); Compose takes dp. The primary part has no native styling target.
macOS SwiftUI/AppKit and Android emulator renderers are verified against the Chrome oracles; iOS runs through the simulator harness; VoiceOver/TalkBack execution remains unverified.

Native Material/Compose appearance; CSS selectors, DOM APIs, browser form APIs, cancelable DOM events and source imperative methods are not compiled. Unsupported source properties are reported by the compiler.
Native RGB sliders, alpha and presets; HEX/RGB output implemented. HSL output and complete source color parsing remain unsupported.

Native Material/Compose appearance; CSS selectors, DOM APIs, browser form APIs, cancelable DOM events and source imperative methods are not compiled. Unsupported source properties are reported by the compiler.

Automatically registers with AWCFormScope for native name/required rules, successful-control data and reset. Declarative text rules use AWCFormRules; native regex/type and browser UI limitations remain explicit.
Uses Material DatePicker; ISO date strings replace JavaScript Date objects in event details.

Dedicated native dialog hosted by AWCModalScope in the app's own viewport (not a platform window): basic (centred alert dialog over a scrim) and fullscreen; all thirteen properties, mdOpen/mdClose/mdCancel in the source order with null payloads, show/close/whenClosed through AWCDialogController, all five slots, ten appearance hooks and eleven typed part targets.

Shared modal layer: one owner stack for dialogs and sheets (only the top owner handles Escape/back, Tab and scrim dismissal; content under an open modal is inert; focus moves in on open and is restored on close, forwarded when a lower owner closes first) and the source z-index paint order, measured against Chrome in thirteen mixed-stack runs.
Outside an AWCModalScope the component keeps the previous platform presentation (a SwiftUI sheet / a Compose dialog window).
macOS SwiftUI/AppKit and Android emulator renderers are verified against the Chrome oracles; iOS SDK, simulator/device and VoiceOver/TalkBack execution remain unverified.

Dedicated native divider uses a measured inner painted line, signed logical inset margins and nonnegative thickness. Inset-start overrides both-side inset; inset-end takes precedence when multiple flags are true. Vertical insets apply at the top and bottom. Native drawing replaces CSS; runtime verification is recorded separately in the parity audit.

Dedicated Compose FAB preserves source sizes, density, seven palettes, labelled extended/collapsed geometry and motion, lowered elevation, disabled state, pointer ripple, keyboard focus and activation. The icon slot retains authored content during controller overrides. mdClick callback detail is null in place of a DOM MouseEvent; scoped AWCActionEvent detail is an empty map and truthful input metadata is available through activation. Android elevation rasterization and native text shaping remain platform-specific. Menu-owned shape/icon-morph choreography is verified with the menu component separately.

SHADOW_DOM.description: Retained named icon composition replaces shadow content. Public typed appearance and measured visual parts replace the five source hooks.
limitations: No DOM nodes or CSS selector engine are exposed.

DOM_QUERY.api: Compose label measurement and named icon composition
DOM_QUERY.description: The actual native text layout supplies label width; retained slot composition supplies current icon content.
limitations: Arbitrary DOM traversal is not reproduced.

SLOT_INTROSPECTION.description: Actual authored slot layout determines fallback presence, including explicit empty Text elements. Temporary menu icons hide rather than discard authored content.
limitations: Native composables replace HTMLElement assignments.

ANIMATION_FRAME.description: The initial target is applied without mount animation. Subsequent extent and label changes use the source spatial and effects curves; native reduced-motion settings disable motion.
limitations: Native frame timing replaces requestAnimationFrame.

DOM_GLOBAL.description: Native layout and font resolution remeasure label width when content, typography or density changes, without document.fonts.
limitations: Native glyph shaping and physical-pixel rounding can differ from browser text rendering.

CANCELABLE_EVENT.description: Cancelable native capture/target/bubble delivery provides actual input metadata; no default action is attached to FAB notification. Callback detail is null; the scoped map is empty.
limitations: DOM MouseEvent and browser propagation objects are not fabricated.

notes: Native nonmodal FAB menu uses AWCFabMenuScope with separately authored ID anchors, actual native bounds, a retained item tree and scoped controller show/close/whenClosed lifecycle. Source input ordering, roving focus, typeahead and typed appearance are implemented; runtime acceptance is recorded separately in audits/md-fab-menu.md. AWCSlotText or AWCSearchableLabelScope supplies actual searchable names for arbitrary native label content. Native scoped appearance restores authored FAB colors on close rather than deleting immutable authored appearance as Web inline-style cleanup does.

DOM_GLOBAL.api: AWCFabMenuScope / authored id and anchor properties
DOM_GLOBAL.description: A scoped native registry resolves authored anchor identity, pointer modality, focus and nonmodal outside activation.
limitations: The scope is the native viewport; global document lookup is not exposed.

DOM_LAYOUT.description: Actual transformed anchor bounds are tracked while open and drive logical-edge positioning and auto placement.
limitations: Native dp replaces browser CSS pixels.

DOM_QUERY.api: Native authored layout-tree traversal / AWCSlotText / AWCSearchableLabelScope
DOM_QUERY.description: Registered item descendants retain authored order for roving focus and typeahead. Explicit native text registration replaces DOM textContent.
limitations: An arbitrary Compose content lambda cannot be introspected for text; use the supplied native searchable-label equivalent.

SHADOW_DOM.api: Composable default slot and nonmodal overlay layer
SHADOW_DOM.description: The retained native layer separates menu flow layout from authored items and anchor.
limitations: No DOM shadow root is created.

CSS_RUNTIME.api: AWCFabMenuAppearanceScope / native layout direction and density
CSS_RUNTIME.description: Typed appearance and applied native geometry replace runtime computed CSS values.
limitations: Arbitrary CSS selectors are not evaluated.

ANIMATION_FRAME.description: Initial paint readiness, cancelable pending opens, delayed close commit and retained cycle completion follow native frame lifecycle.
limitations: Native frame scheduling replaces requestAnimationFrame.

CANCELABLE_EVENT.description: Void lifecycle callbacks and synchronous scoped capture/target/bubble events preserve committed-state ordering.
limitations: DOM event objects are not fabricated.

notes: Dedicated native menu item supports all six properties, icon and fallback label slots, actual density geometry, native ripple and roving focus. Void mdClick callbacks use null; scoped event detail is an empty map with truthful activation metadata. Native text shaping remains platform-specific; runtime acceptance is recorded separately in the menu audit.

SLOT_INTROSPECTION.description: Actual authored icon content, including explicit empty Text, controls icon fallback and padding.
limitations: Native composition replaces assignedElements.

CANCELABLE_EVENT.description: Cancelable synchronous native delivery preserves pointer and keyboard metadata and allows propagation to the parent menu to be stopped.
limitations: DOM MouseEvent and KeyboardEvent are not fabricated.

notes: Dedicated Compose renderer implements all 19 source properties, all five size and density rungs, narrow/default/wide widths, four source palettes, selected/pressed/resting morph precedence, connected logical corners, pointer-origin ripple, keyboard focus and native group coordination. Default/selected slots replace glyph fallbacks; direct native badges adorn without suppressing the icon and avatars retain their own dimensions. Navigation and toggle commit before cancelable mdClick notification, exactly as the source does; no mdChange is emitted. The nine public CSS hooks map to AWCIconButtonAppearance. Native layout evidence covers the visual root, state-layer and active icon part. Source DOM objects, CSS selector evaluation, browser windows and forced-colors media queries remain platform-specific.

SHADOW_DOM.description: Default and selected composable slots replace source glyphs. Direct native badges and avatars preserve their source slot sizing roles.
limitations: Native composition replaces shadow DOM; arbitrary DOM inspection is not exposed.

DOM_QUERY.description: Native slot lookup and injected application routing replace the component-specific DOM queries.
limitations: No arbitrary CSS selector engine or browser window is created.

SLOT_INTROSPECTION.description: Subcomposition detects actual child layout and selects the default or selected icon layer; badges do not count as replacement icons. Explicit Text composables, including empty editor text, represent authored replacement elements.
limitations: Compose children replace DOM nodes; omission restores fallback while an authored empty element suppresses it.

DOM_GLOBAL.description: Safe relative links resolve against the source native context current URL. Observable native contexts implement self, blank, parent, top and reusable named destinations, independent history, back and subtree close. A host can reject navigation before commit and present accepted destinations after commit. Unsafe raw links never fall through to form actions.
limitations: Contexts are native application state, not browser windows, documents, origins or opener relationships; no page is fetched by the coordinator.

Named native destinations are deliberately reusable; source window.open with noopener/noreferrer may instead create fresh browser contexts. Browser modifier/middle-click navigation and window APIs are not reproduced.
URLs must parse as native URIs. Applications supply presentation for coordinator destinations; the legacy default router still opens absolute Android URIs.

CANCELABLE_EVENT.description: Scoped native capture/target/bubble delivery exposes cancelable mdClick after safe navigation and selection have already committed, matching the source icon-button ordering.
limitations: Calling preventDefault marks the notification but cannot undo effects that preceded it. OS input and DOM propagation are not fabricated.

notes: Dedicated native chart (the ported md-chart engine drawn on a SwiftUI Canvas / Compose DrawScope): every property, the legend, tooltips, hover layer, keyboard cursor and its live announcement, drag and slider zoom, entrance / drill / follow motion, the header, footer, empty and loader slots, and every event.

Formatter and renderer closures (valueFormatter, tooltipRenderer) go through AWCChartFormatters + .awcChartFormatters (SwiftUI) / ChartFormatters + LocalAWCChartFormatters (Compose), keyed by node id; hooks through AWCChartAppearance; methods through AWCChartController (toDataURL returns the canvas layer as a PNG data URL; getInstance has no native counterpart — it returns the Web engine object).

macOS SwiftUI, the iOS simulator and the Android emulator are verified against Chrome 153: paint scenes, hover / keyboard / pointer and state replays with events, entrance motion per frame, slots, RTL.

Dedicated native list: all eight properties (list, listbox with single/multi selection, menu and other role overrides, density 0…−4), mdSelect, mdActivate and mdReorder with the source payloads (item references become stable native node IDs), the four methods through AWCListController, ten appearance hooks and the drop-placeholder part.

Roving focus with wrap, Home/End and 500 ms typeahead; pointer reorder from the drag handle (lift, sibling shift, dashed placeholder glide, drop) and Alt+Arrow keyboard reorder, measured against Chrome frame by frame.
A reorder keeps the authored composition and translates rows to their displayed slots; on Compose the accessibility order follows the authored order until the host applies mdReorder.
macOS SwiftUI/AppKit and Android emulator renderers are verified against the Chrome oracles; iOS SDK, simulator/device and VoiceOver/TalkBack execution remain unverified.

Dedicated native list item: all twenty-eight properties (the list-managed ones — tabbable, rovingFocusVisible, selectionMode, interactionMode, containerRole, reorderable — follow the parent list as in the source), mdClick and mdExpand with the source payloads and order, the five methods through AWCListItemController, all eight slots, sixty-eight appearance hooks and twenty-seven typed part targets.

mdItemClick, mdItemSelect, mdRequestActivation and mdItemRequestReorder are the source's internal item-to-list protocol; natively the list coordinates its rows directly and emits mdSelect, mdActivate and mdReorder instead.

Accessibility: a selection row is an option with its selected state (a radio button in a single-select listbox, a checkbox in a multi-select one), a menu row is a menu item (a button on Compose), the primary action is a button or link; the row's index is its set position. The headline and supporting text use the shared md-tooltip while clipped.
The headline-tooltip-popup and supporting-tooltip-popup parts are styled through the shared md-tooltip appearance, not the list item part API.
macOS SwiftUI/AppKit and Android emulator renderers are verified against the Chrome oracles; iOS SDK, simulator/device and VoiceOver/TalkBack execution remain unverified.

Dedicated native polygon animation preserves source geometry, colors, density, clipping, exact keyframes and typed corner radii. AWCLoadingIndicatorShapeAppearanceScope styles the measured shape part. Android animation preference supplies reduced motion; explicit AWCAccessibilityAppearanceScope forcedColors is a native environment override, not inferred from system contrast. No default tabstop is added; caller focus modifiers opt into native focus. Runtime verification is recorded separately.

Dedicated native renderer (SwiftUI / Compose): the baseline, standard and vibrant surfaces, the standard and grouped (gap) layouts, the header slot, empty text, density, a capped scrolling viewport (max-height, --md-menu-max-block-size) and the 150 ms scale-and-fade entrance and exit (quick and Reduce Motion snap), verified against the Mac Chrome 153 oracles (paint, interaction states and motion).

Anchored menus present in the nearest AWCMenuScope (the menus' top layer): bottom/top-start/end placement against the anchor's live frame (physical, as the source), flipped and kept inside the viewport margin, match-anchor-width and the responsive full-width surface. Outside a scope a menu renders in flow.

Source behaviour: auto-focus of the first row, roving focus with typeahead, Escape and Tab close the tree and restore focus to the anchor, outside clicks close non-persistent menus, opening a menu closes its open peers; mdOpen / mdClose as the source. listbox exposes the surface as a listbox of options.

show({ autoFocus }), close(), whenClosed() and reposition() through AWCMenuScopeState.menu(id); getScrollViewport() returns the viewport geometry (scrollTop, scrollHeight, clientHeight) rather than an element. setComboboxElement() and setVirtualProvider() are the DOM combobox and virtualization plumbing of md-select / md-autocomplete and have no native counterpart.
The six menu hooks and the five row hooks (inherited by every row) through .awcMenuAppearance(…) / AWCMenuAppearanceScope.

Rendered by its md-menu: one- and two-line rows with the leading-icon and trailing-icon slots, trailing text, badge, divider and gap, checkbox and radio rows (check position, indeterminate, keep-open), option presentation and role override, density; hover, press and keyboard focus show the state layer, the md-ripple wave and the inset 3-point focus ring.

Activation emits mdClick and closes the menu tree after 150 ms unless keep-open; Space toggles checkbox and radio rows without closing; disabled rows stay focusable in the roving order (APG) but inert.
A labelled group (role group) with its label row; the grouped layout of its md-menu draws it as a card; density as the source.

Dedicated read-only Compose meter supports the fourteen source properties, native ICU locale formatting and seven typed appearance hooks. AWCMeterRangeKey retains the exact Double range alongside Android accessibility range data. Native paths, shaped text and measured visual parts replace SVG and CSS. Runtime verification is recorded separately in the parity audit.

Dedicated native renderer (SwiftUI / Compose): chips (bottom / top / sides / inline with count or wrap overflow), the button trigger, select-all, max-selected, filterable search, clear and remove, on the md-menu listbox; verified against the Mac Chrome 153 oracles (paint 1222 checks; interaction states, full and reduced).
Not supported: virtualize (not virtualized: the native lists render every option (loadOptions / options replace the list)).
Not supported: filterMode (filtering is local (contains); the source's remote mode is the app's (setQuery / loadOptions)).
Not supported: rowHeight (virtualization row height (no virtualized list)).
Not supported: countFormatter (a JavaScript function value).
Not supported: searchingLabel (remote-search status text (no remote mode)).

Dedicated native renderer (SwiftUI / Compose): the full-width row of equal destinations (flex 1 1 0, min 64), surface-container, the density-tapered 64-point height, the top divider, corners and elevation hooks, computed from the authored md-navigation-tab children as the source.

Selection as the source: activeIndex is truncated and clamped to an activatable destination (forward, then backward; −1 when none); clicks, Enter/Space, the arrows (automatic activation unless manualActivation; mirrored in RTL; soft-disabled destinations reachable but never activated), Home/End, activeIndex writes and select(index) emit mdChange { index, previousIndex } when the selection changes.

One tab stop (the active destination); focusTab(index) focuses without selecting. labelBehavior (always / selected / none) passes to destinations without their own value. Reduced motion removes the transitions (the ripple stays).

Forms: registers with the native form (name, value, constraint validation, reset without events); Enter submits a single-line field's form. Speech-to-text internal mode uses the platform recognizer (SFSpeechRecognizer with the app's usage descriptions; Android SpeechRecognizer with RECORD_AUDIO); external mode reports the microphone state.

macOS SwiftUI, the iOS simulator and the Android emulator are verified against Chrome 153 (paint incl. ::part cases, per-frame motion, events and timing). On iOS a tap focuses on release (UIKit convention), so the focus motion starts one tap later than Chrome's mouse press.

Native Material/Compose appearance; CSS selectors, DOM APIs, browser form APIs, cancelable DOM events and source imperative methods are not compiled. Unsupported source properties are reported by the compiler.

Automatically registers with AWCFormScope for native name/required rules, successful-control data and reset. Declarative text rules use AWCFormRules; native regex/type and browser UI limitations remain explicit.
Uses Material TimePicker; dialog native layout replaces docked web variants.

Dedicated native toolbar (SwiftUI / Compose): docked bar and floating pill (horizontal or vertical), standard / vibrant colours, the leading / default / trailing sections with their gaps and alignment, the paired FAB, density, and the opt-in scrolling / wrapping overflow, computed from the authored children as the source.

Roving focus over the icon buttons and buttons (one Tab stop, arrows on the bar's axis, Home / End, wrap; soft-disabled members reachable, hidden / disabled / aria-hidden ones skipped; other controls keep their own stop), re-synced when children change; the toolbar-only icon-button tints; role toolbar with orientation and name, or a generic container.
Hooks through .awcToolbarAppearance(…) / AWCToolbarAppearanceScope; setFocus() through AWCToolbarController.

macOS SwiftUI, the iOS simulator and the Android emulator are verified against Mac Chrome 153: paint and geometry of every configuration, roving focus, Tab order, the dynamic re-sync, pointer state layers, RTL and density.
Dedicated native anchor and overlay scope retain all twelve properties, four content outlets, two lifecycle methods, eleven appearance hooks and five typed part targets.
Source mdOpen/mdClose events have null detail and are cancelable, non-bubbling and non-composed: same-tree capture and target listeners run; cancellation does not undo committed visibility.
Public typed slots, part styles and measured overlay coordinates replace DOM selectors, shadow slots and computed CSS. Arbitrary native content keeps its own handlers and explicitly authored layout.
The native overlay scope must cover the intended viewport. Hover/focus delays, grace periods, RTL placement, flipping, clamping, Escape ownership and retained updates are implemented.
Android Compose rendering, authored callbacks, focus/hover, event boundary and retained-host checks are recorded; TalkBack delivery and OS accessibility traversal remain unverified.
